children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rebounded sharply from nine-month lows on Tuesday, as chipmakers tracked overnight gains in US tech stocks
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 220.28 points, or 4.39%, at 5,239.13. On Monday, it closed at the lowest level since February 2
** US stocks rallied on Monday, as a drop in oil prices tempered inflation fears and tech shares jumped even as AI heavyweight Nvidia
slumped with controversy swirling around CEO Jensen Huang
** "The domestic market tracked sharp gains in US chip stocks on dip buying, while lower oil prices also supported market sentiment," said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 4.74%, while peer SK Hynix
gained 6.69%
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 3.93%, while Hyundai Motor
was up 1.29% and sister automaker Kia Corp
was down 0.93%
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
added 4.63%, while drugmaker Samsung Biologics
fell 2.78%.
** Of the total 911 traded issues, 716 shares advanced, while 175 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 390.7 billion won ($291.09 million)
** The won was quoted at 1,337.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.19% higher than its previous close at 1,340.0
** In money and debt markets, December futures on 3-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.01 point to 103.82
** The most liquid 3-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 0.2 basis points to 3.636%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 0.7 basis points to 3.851%
KOSPI rises, foreigners net buyers
